paper.title_en: Latency-Preserving Rewrites and Translation Validation for Dynamic Quantum Circuits
paper.abstract_en: A dynamic quantum circuit measures qubits during a run and chooses later operations from the outcomes. These branches make the qubits wait: the outcome must reach the classical controller, and the controller must decide. We present qlin, a compiler that reduces this waiting time. qlin moves operations out of branches without delaying the program, a property proved in Lean 4. For error-correction decoders, which branch on syndromes that are almost always zero, qlin compiles the likely syndromes into one multiway branch and keeps the original program for the rest. A cost model decides when a classically controlled gate should become a quantum-controlled gate instead. On all benchmarks, qlin checks that the compiled program computes what its source computes, and the checker is proved sound in Lean 4. At the published per-decision cost of the QICK controller (42 ns), 10 of 65 programs run at least 10% faster than the best baseline in our cost model, up to 91.2%, mostly because one multiway branch replaces a long chain of if statements. On the register-transfer logic of the QubiC controller, a compiled distance-5 repetition decoder selects its correction in 21.3 instead of 151.1 expected cycles. Timing runs on an IBM device were too noisy to confirm or reject the model's ranking.
